issue.title: glob_files misses untracked files in subdirectories when searching from the workspace root

steps: Run git init -q, create src/tracked.txt containing tracked and src/untracked.txt containing untracked, then git add src/tracked.txt only. Leave src/untracked.txt untracked.
Use glob_files with pattern="**/*.txt" and path=".". Then repeat with pattern="**/*.txt" and path="src". Report both raw tool results.
expected: Both root and scoped searches include src/untracked.txt.
defect: Root discovery lists tracked files plus only root-level untracked files, missing the untracked file under src/.

fault location.explanation: The root search keeps include_untracked=false and uses git ls-files --cached. mergeRootUntrackedCandidates only scans direct root children; scoped roots use recursive fallback and find the same file.

Root cause: The root search keeps include_untracked=false and uses git ls-files --cached. mergeRootUntrackedCandidates only scans direct root children; scoped roots use recursive fallback and find the same file.

_meta.notes: Exact minimal structure from the issue. A Git commit is unnecessary; git add establishes a tracked index entry. The issue was created 2026-08-21; v0.0.4 has the exact include_untracked/scoped-root and direct-child merge implementation cited by the report. The current v0.0.14 source has been refactored and no longer contains that helper, so this case freezes the source-confirmed v0.0.4 release rather than assuming the old mechanism still exists at the pin.
